Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

DURBAN, South Africa -- India's Yuvraj Singh smashed six sixes in one over as England crashed out of cricket's World Twenty20 tournament in South Africa on Wednesday. Yuvraj Singh smashes his sixth successive six off England fast bowler Stuart Broad . Paul Collingwood's side were eliminated at the Super Eights stage after South Africa earlier beat New Zealand by six wickets in Durban. England then lost by 18 runs to the Singh-inspired Indians, who kept their semifinal hopes alive ahead of Thursday's must-win clash with the hosts. Singh reached the fastest 50 in Twenty20 history, needing just 12 deliveries, as India made 218-4. The left-hander's six consecutive sixes in the 19th over bowled by Stuart Broad made him the first player to do so in Twenty20 matches and just the fourth in all senior cricket. South Africa's Herschelle Gibbs performed the feat at the 50-over World Cup in the West Indies earlier this year, while Sir Garfield Sobers and Ravi Shastri achieved it in first-class matches. Singh's innings ended on 58 -- from 16 balls -- when he hit a full-toss from Andrew Flintoff to captain Collingwood at long-on from the penultimate delivery of the final over, in which he also cleared the boundary ropes once. Virender Sehwag top-scored with 68 off 52 balls, putting on 136 for the first wicket with Gautam Gambhir, who hit 58 off 41 deliveries. Broad ended with the embarrassing figures of 0-60 off his four overs, while fellow seamer Chris Tremlett took 2-45. In reply, England battled gamely but could only post 200-6 in their 20 overs. Opener Vikram Solanki top-scored with 43 off 31 balls, and Kevin Pietersen hit 39 off 23 deliveries, but no-one could match the fireworks provided by Singh. Left-arm seamer Irfan Pathan claimed figures of 3-37 off four overs, while Rudra Pratap Singh took 2-28. If India can beat South Africa, it would create a three-way tie and require net run-rates to decide the two teams going through. The Proteas have two wins from two Group E outings after beating New Zealand, who have completed their Super Eights fixtures with two victories and a defeat. South Africa restricted the Black Caps to 153-8 from their 20 overs on Wednesday, then reached the target with five deliveries to spare as Justin Kemp made an unbeaten 89. Kemp was named man of the match after smashing a six off the otherwise economical Mark Gillespie for the winning runs. He belted six sixes and six fours in his 56-ball innings, having come to the crease in the fourth over with South Africa reeling at 17-2. Kemp added 28 in four overs with Gibbs (19) before putting on another 65 in eight overs with Mark Boucher. Boucher departed for 23, caught by wicketkeeper Brendon McCullum off Gillespie, who ended with figures of 2-11 off 3.1 overs. The experienced Shaun Pollock then joined Kemp, and struck one six in his unbeaten 16 off 11 deliveries to help guide the Proteas to their second victory. The in-form Craig McMillan top-scored for the Kiwis, hitting an unbeaten 48 off only 25 balls to follow up his blistering 57 in Tuesday's five-run win against England. McCullum had put on 68 for the first wicket with Lou Vincent, scoring 38 before becoming the first of Morne Morkel's four victims. Morkel, who ended with figures of 4-17 off four overs, then removed Ross Taylor (1) two runs later and later bowled the dangerous Jacob Oram for a quickfire 15. He had Shane Bond caught by Boucher, and then almost became the first Twenty20 bowler to claim five wickets when his penultimate delivery -- which clean bowled Gillespie -- was declared a no-ball by umpire Billy Doctrove. ## World Twenty20 Super Eights — 19 September 2007, Durban

### South Africa beat New Zealand by six wickets

**New Zealand 153/8 (20 overs)**  
- Craig McMillan 48 from 25 balls  
- Lou Vincent 32  
- Peter Fulton 32  
- Shaun Pollock was exceptionally economical, conceding only 17 runs in four overs.  
- Makhaya Ntini and Albie Morkel took two wickets apiece.

**South Africa 158/4 (19.1 overs)**  
- Justin Kemp **89 not out from 56 balls**, with six fours and six sixes  
- Mark Boucher **23 not out**  
- Kyle Mills took two wickets; Shane Bond and Daniel Vettori took one each.

**Result:** South Africa won by six wickets with five balls remaining.

South Africa were in trouble at roughly 45/4 before Kemp and Boucher added an unbroken 112. Kemp dominated the chase, combining forceful straight hitting with patience against Vettori. The win gave South Africa two victories from two Super Eight matches and left them strongly placed, although not yet mathematically safe because net run rate could still come into play.

---

### India beat England by 18 runs

**India 218/4 (20 overs)**  
- Virender Sehwag 68 from 52 balls  
- Gautam Gambhir 58 from 41  
- Yuvraj Singh **58 from 16 balls**  
- Andrew Flintoff 2 wickets  
- Chris Tremlett 2 wickets  
- Stuart Broad: **4-0-60-0**

Sehwag and Gambhir put on 136 for the first wicket, establishing the platform for one of the tournament’s defining innings. Yuvraj reached fifty from **12 balls**, then the fastest half-century in senior international cricket.

In Broad’s 19th over, Yuvraj hit all six deliveries for six:

**6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6**

It was the first six-sixes over in a Twenty20 international and only the fourth such occurrence in senior top-level cricket at the time. Yuvraj finished with three fours and seven sixes.

**England 200/6 (20 overs)**  
- Vikram Solanki 43  
- Kevin Pietersen 39 from 23 balls  
- Paul Collingwood 28  
- Owais Shah 21 not out  
- Irfan Pathan: **4-0-37-3**  
- R.P. Singh: **4-0-28-2**  
- Harbhajan Singh: **4-0-35-1**

**Result:** India won by 18 runs.

England’s chase remained competitive through Solanki and Pietersen, but regular wickets prevented a sustained late assault. Pathan removed three of England’s top and middle-order batters, while R.P. Singh’s 2/28 provided the best economy among India’s seamers.

---

## Semifinal qualification picture

After the two September 19 matches, **England were eliminated**, having lost all three of their Super Eight games.

The Group E table was effectively:

- **South Africa:** 4 points from 2 matches  
- **New Zealand:** 4 points from 3 matches  
- **India:** 2 points from 2 matches  
- **England:** 0 points from 3 matches  

Everything therefore rested on the final group match, **South Africa v India on September 20**:

- **If South Africa won**, South Africa and New Zealand would qualify.
- **India had to win** to reach the semifinals.
- An Indian victory would create a three-way tie on four points among India, South Africa and New Zealand, with **net run rate** deciding the two qualifiers.
- South Africa’s strong net run rate gave them considerable protection, but a sufficiently heavy defeat could still eliminate them.
- New Zealand, having completed their fixtures, needed South Africa to beat India—or otherwise needed the net-run-rate calculations to fall in their favor.

India eventually won that final match by 37 runs, qualifying alongside New Zealand and knocking South Africa out on net run rate.

## Cricket news recap — 19 September 2007

Yuvraj Singh produced one of cricket’s most explosive innings as India defeated England in a run-filled ICC World Twenty20 Super Eight match in Durban, while Justin Kemp’s unbeaten 89 guided South Africa past New Zealand at the same venue.

### Yuvraj’s 12-ball fifty powers India to 218-4

India, needing a win to keep their semi-final hopes alive, piled up **218 for four** after captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni chose to bat.

Openers **Virender Sehwag** and **Gautam Gambhir** laid the foundation with a 136-run partnership. Sehwag struck **68 from 52 balls**, while Gambhir made **58 from 41**. England briefly slowed India after dismissing both openers, but Yuvraj transformed the innings at the death.

Following a heated exchange with Andrew Flintoff, Yuvraj attacked Stuart Broad in the 19th over and hit **all six deliveries for six**. He became only the fourth player in senior cricket to achieve the feat and the first to do so in a Twenty20 international.

The sixes came to different parts of Kingsmead:

1. Over cow corner  
2. A flick behind square leg  
3. Over extra cover  
4. Sliced over backward point  
5. A huge leg-side blow  
6. Over long-on  

Yuvraj reached his fifty from **12 balls**, then the fastest half-century in any form of international cricket. He was dismissed for **58 from only 16 deliveries**, having struck **seven sixes and three fours**. India scored 58 from the final three overs to finish on 218-4.

England mounted a respectable chase but never quite matched the required rate. **Vikram Solanki made 43**, **Kevin Pietersen scored 39**, and captain **Paul Collingwood added 28**, but regular wickets kept India in control. England closed on **200 for six**, giving India an **18-run victory**.

Irfan Pathan was India’s most successful bowler with three wickets, while RP Singh took two. Yuvraj was named player of the match.

His 12-ball fifty remained the fastest in men’s T20 internationals until Nepal’s Dipendra Singh Airee reached fifty from nine balls in 2023. It remains the fastest fifty in a T20 World Cup.

---

## Kemp rescues South Africa against New Zealand

Earlier in Durban, **Justin Kemp hit an unbeaten 89** as South Africa chased down New Zealand’s **153 for eight**.

New Zealand’s innings was driven by aggressive contributions from **Craig McMillan, who made 48**, and **Jacob Oram, who scored 35**. South African fast bowler **Morne Morkel took four wickets for 17 runs**, preventing New Zealand from building a larger total.

South Africa’s reply began badly. The hosts lost early wickets and slipped to **45 for four**, leaving New Zealand firmly in control. Kemp then rebuilt the innings alongside wicketkeeper **Mark Boucher**.

Kemp mixed patience with powerful hitting, finishing on **89 not out from 56 balls**, with six fours and six sixes. Boucher provided the support with an unbeaten 23 as the pair added **112 without being separated** for the fifth wicket.

South Africa reached **158 for four in 19.1 overs**, winning by **six wickets with five balls remaining**. Kemp’s innings earned him the player-of-the-match award and preserved South Africa’s unbeaten record in the tournament at that stage.

### Scores at a glance

- **India 218-4** beat **England 200-6** by 18 runs  
  - Yuvraj Singh 58 from 16 balls; fifty from 12 balls  
  - Six sixes in one Stuart Broad over  

- **New Zealand 153-8** lost to **South Africa 158-4** by six wickets  
  - Justin Kemp 89 not out from 56 balls  
  - Morne Morkel 4-17  
  - South Africa won with five balls remaining  

The day is remembered above all for Yuvraj’s assault on Broad—one of the defining moments of the inaugural World Twenty20 and one of the most famous overs in cricket history.
